focus.note: Many verbs and adjectives need a fixed preposition after them. Check the word before the gap, then ask which preposition always goes with it.

tfn.s: The writer implies that GTA VI's day-one figure and Endgame's opening measure different things.
tfn.why: A film's opening shows how many people turned up; a game's day one shows how much people were willing to pay.

tfn.s: The Sensor Tower estimate is presented as proof that Take-Two overstated its sales.
tfn.why: The text says it was measuring "something different at a different moment".

tfn.s: Take-Two has said when the next GTA Online will be released.
tfn.why: The text only says an analyst thinks the timing of the next GTA Online matters.

tfn.s: According to the text, the day-one total may include demand built up before launch.
tfn.why: The text says "we cannot tell how much of the total was a first-day rush and how much was demand built up over months".

tfn.s: The writer argues that a big budget removes the need to keep earning after day one.
tfn.why: The text says a game that costs so much "must keep earning long after the first day".

speak.title: Role-play: buy it now or wait?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: A big new game comes out today. You want to buy it now, on the first day. Explain why you can't wait and try to persuade your friend to buy it too.

b.text: You think it's better to wait. Ask about the price, the reviews and the other things you could spend the money on. Decide if you will buy it.

phrases: I can't wait any longer, it's out today!
Why don't we read some reviews first?
It's a lot of money for one game.
That's a fair point, but I'd hate to miss out.
What would you do with the money instead?
Let's wait a week and then decide.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: who was more convincing, and did your friend buy the game on the first day?
